notes:
CHR-618/CHR-621 ticket state 7 (zoomed out half), corrected after a second CTO review: the previous version (42 tiles at 17% zoom) contradicted its own "Fit all" toolbar state — 42 tiles at 17% would only fill a small fraction of the canvas, not the whole thing. Fixed by making the project the size Christian actually named (186 screens) and computing the zoom honestly instead of picking a number that looked dramatic.

**Arithmetic (stated per CTO's request):**
- Native (100%) tile: 180px wide, ~150px tall including its name row (`$board-tile` `default` variant: 120px thumb + ~30px name-wrap).
- Board's available canvas area at this screen's fixed 1440×900 frame: 1404×812 (topbar 48px, toolbar 40px, 36px collapsed sidebar rail), minus `$spacing.2xl` (24px) padding on all sides of the grid → 1356×764 usable for tiles.
- Solving for an integer column/row grid whose tile count is close to 186 and whose footprint fills that area: 17 columns × 11 rows = 187 cells; drop one tile from the last (partial) row → exactly 186, matching Christian's real project.
- Mini tile width from the width equation: `17w + 16×4px(gap) = 1356` → `w ≈ 75.6px` → 76px.
- Honest zoom = mini tile width ÷ native tile width = `76 ÷ 180 ≈ 0.42` → **42%**.
- Height check: mini tile height scaled by the same factor, `150 × 0.42 ≈ 63px`; `11×63 + 10×4 = 733px` against the 764px budget — a small (~4%) vertical margin from the grid not dividing evenly, not a contradiction of "edge to edge."
- `$board-toolbar`'s `fitall-edgesoff` variant and `$zoom-slider`'s `min` variant were both updated to show 42% (thumb at `(42−10)/190×140 ≈ 24px` along the track) — they previously showed 17%, left over from the very first draft; nothing else references that low-zoom variant, so it was safe to redefine in place rather than adding a second one.

**CORRECTION (implementation measurement, post-approval):** this screen's 42% is mock arithmetic only, built on this design's simplified 180px fixed-size tile and a fixed 1440×900 frame. The real board's tiles are 390×844 (actual screen proportions) and its column count is computed to fit the real viewport (see `chr621-continuous-zoom-slider` decision and `chr-621` tag notes) — on Christian's actual 186-screen project the true fit-all scale measured out to ~7.6%, which is why the slider floor moved from 10% to 5%. Do not treat 42% as the real number; it only demonstrates that a large project needs a low zoom to fit, not what that zoom actually is.

**Labels**: this screen sits at 42%, inside the truncated band under my original 20% threshold — but 42% scaled body text (`typography.size-xs` ≈12.5px × 0.42 ≈ 5.2px) is well under any legible floor, so labels are hidden entirely here too. This exposed that the original "<20% hidden" threshold was too low to be honest about legibility; see the updated `chr621-continuous-zoom-slider` design-system decision, which now cites the font-size math instead of a round guessed number.

**Component promotion**: at 186 repeats the tile card was clearly overdue for `promote_to_system` — built as `$board-tile` `mini` variant (see its own usage notes). `board-view` and `board-view-presented` were also migrated to `$board-tile` (`default` / `outside-filter` variants) in the same pass so all three screens share one tile component instead of one promoted + two still-inline.

Edges are off (`fitall-edgesoff`), five tiles carry the `$pin-button` `pinned` marker (scaled to 14px) scattered through the grid — still individually findable as small blue dots even in a nearly edge-to-edge field of 186 tiles, which is the point of this screen.
